previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, recurrent cellulitis, PTSD, and depression was admitted with fever, myalgias, and diarrhea, followed by shortness of breath and left lower lobe pneumonia on chest X-ray. She was treated with ceftriaxone and azithromycin for bacterial pneumonia, while viral syndrome was considered the likely cause of her systemic symptoms. Stool studies were negative for C. diff, Salmonella, Shigella, and other pathogens, and blood cultures showed no growth. On hospital day 2, she developed transient volume overload with pleural effusions, likely due to IV fluids, which resolved after diuresis with Lasix. Her symptoms gradually improved, fever resolved, and she was discharged home on oral antibiotics with plans to complete a 7-day course. She remained on minocycline for stable leg cellulitis, continued her home medications, and was advised to follow up with her primary care and infectious disease providers.

# Strep Viridans bacteremia: Blood cultures obtained in the ED 
were positive for Strep Viridans in 2 out of 2 bottles.  One of 
the bottles was also positive for gram positive rods which was 
thought to be a contaminant.  The patient was started on 
vancomycin initially until the culture and sensitivities 
returned.  THe patient was then switched to ceftriaxone given 
her penicilin allergy (she previously tolerated ceftriaxone).  
Serial blood cultures were drawn and were negative.  The patient 
had a TTE and a TEE both of which did not show evidence of 
endocarditis.  A panorex film was obtained and revealed a 
possible abscess near her right lower ___ bicuspid tooth.  This 
was thought to be the source of the bacteremia.  The patient was 
taken to surgery for tooth exxtraction.  She remained on 
ceftriaxone Q 12 hr.  48 hrs following the tooth extraction she 
had a PICC line placed for further IV administration of 
ceftriaxone.  She will need to continue to get Ceftriaxone Q 12 
hr for 14 days after ___.  She will need to follow up with 
infectious disease who will then decide if she will need to 
continue antibiotic therapy with an oral antibiotic tail.
.
# Reactive airways disease: The patient presented with symptoms 
of cough, chest tightness, and shortness of breath.  This was 
thought to be likely post viral reactive airways disease given 
history of previous viral induced asthma and recent PNA.  She 
was started  on a steroid inhaler and nebulizers as well as 
antitussive medications.  Her lungs were clear to auscultation 
throughout most of her hospitalization.  She should continue the 
fluticasone inhaler as an outpatient.  
.
# Nausea/diarrhea: The patient complained of some mild nausea 
and loose stools thought to be due to the ceftriaxone given the 
time course.  She was checked for C diff which was negative x 1. 
 LFTs were normal.  She noted having similar symptoms last time 
she was in the hospital receiving Ceftriaxone. Her diarrhea was 
improving prior to discharge.
.
# Atrial fibrilation: The patient was noted to have brief 
paroxysmal a fib overnight. Episodes were too brief to capture 
on EKG, but were seen on telemetry.  A TSH was checked and was 
normal.  This was thought to be due to infection.  There was no 
need for anticoagulation with coumadin given lack of risk 
factors and transient a fib in setting of infection.
.
# Sinus Tachycardia: The patient presented with tachycardia in 
the setting of frequent albuterol use and deconditioning from 
recent hospitalization.  The tachycardia was thought to be from 
a combination of the two in addition to some mild volume 
depletion.  CTA was negative for PE.  She was given a small 
bolus of IV fluids and her tachycardia improved.  When her 
inhaler requirement decreased, her tachycardia improved as well.
.
# Bradycardia: Occurred while sleeping on ___ and again on 
___.  Was thought to be sleep apnea causing bradycardia. 
Continuous O2 monitoring revealed desats. Endocarditis ruled out 
with negative TEE.
The patient is being discharged with home O2 to be worn by nasal 
canula at bedtime.  She will need an outpatient sleep study to 
confirm a diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea.
.
# Diarrhea: Extensively evaluated on last admission with no 
clear infectious source. C diff negative.  Was thought to be in 
part from ceftriaxone.  Was given loperamide.
.
# Anemia: Was found to have low MCV. Fe studies were not c/w 
iron defficiency anemia.  The patient's Hct subsequently 
improved.
.
# Leftward deviation of the trachea at the thoracic inlet: Seen 
incidentally on CXR. TSH was checked and was normal.  The 
patient should have her PCP set her up for an ultrasound as an 
outpatient.
.
# Chronic ___ dermatosclerosis: There were no signs of acute 
cellulitis or DVT.  The patient was continued on her home dose 
minocycline.
.

INDICATION:  IV access needed for antibiotics.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right basilic
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access are on file.  A peel-away sheath was then
placed over a guidewire and a double-lumen PICC line measuring 41 cm in length
was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the
SVC under fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided 5 ___
double-lumen PICC line placement via the right basilic venous approach.  Final
internal length is 41 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC.  The line is ready
to use.
